messages:
alex: main pipeline turned red after that merge — gpu-inference-smoke is failing in kernel init. link: https://ci.redwood/reports/742 (job gpu-inference-smoke)
ci-bot: AUTORUN: pipeline failed on branch main — job gpu-inference-smoke (build 742) — status: FAIL\n\nalex: quick log snippet:\n```\n[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] ERROR allocate_gpu_memory: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] FATAL kernel_init.cc:88: failed to initialize kernels: out of memory
```\nmorgan: @alex is this the merge from #3127 (runtime: bump default batch to 8)?
alex: yeah that one. suspected change is the batch default in runtime-config. but the failure is during kernel compile / init, before any request. looks like provisioned instance couldn't satisfy memory. :thinking:
ravi: can someone rerun the failed job first? if it's infra flake the rerun will pass and we avoid revert.
alex: @ci-bot can you trigger a rerun for build 742? (or point me to the rerun command)
ci-bot: To rerun the job: go to the job page and click "Rerun failed" or run: `cictl rerun --job gpu-inference-smoke --build 742`\nI queued a retry request.
sam: pinging infra on-call @morgan in case it's an instance provisioning hiccup — we've seen spot instances come up undersized earlier today. :eyes:
morgan: looking at cloud logs — one of the gpus spun up with 4GB less than expected due to a SKU mismatch. provisioning handed vGPU-8 instead of vGPU-12 for that runner. still investigating why the flavor mapping drifted.
alex: thanks. @ravi if rerun passes can we mark as flake and hold on revert? if rerun fails again we should bisect / revert quickly.
ravi: sounds good. if rerun fails twice, I'll start a bisect and tag owners.
ci-bot: Retry result: build 742 retry #1 -> PASSED (gpu-inference-smoke).\n
alex: ok retry passed :thumbsup: — keeping open for 30m to watch for recurrence. filing follow-up to harden runner flavor mapping and add explicit SKUs to CI pools (ticket: INFRA-589).
sam: can we also add a pre-check that validates GPU mem visible in runner before running heavy kernel tests? simple gate: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total --format=csv` — if <X, mark job as infra-flake and skip.
morgan: good idea, will prototype check.
alex: thanks all. closing this thread unless it flips again. :raised_hands:
